title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and the risk of thyroid cancer
authors: Bezin J, Gouverneur A, Pénichon M, Mathieu C, Garrel R, Hillaire-Buys D, et al.
followUp: exposure measured over 6 years before a 6-month lag; cancers identified 2014 to 2018
population: Nested case-control analysis in the French national health insurance database (SNDS) of people with type 2 diabetes on second-line antidiabetic drugs from 2006 to 2018: 2562 thyroid cancer cases matched to 45,184 controls
funder: This work was supported by the French Medicines Agency (Agence Nationale de Sécurité du Médicament et des Produits de Santé, ANSM, grant 2019S015) in the context of a partnership with the Health Product Epidemiology Scientific Interest Group (EPI-PHARE), as part of the DRUGS-SAFER research programme. The French Medicines Agency played no role in the study design or conduct or results interpretation or discussion.
authorConflicts: All authors declare support from the French Medicines Agency for the submitted work; no other potential conflicts of interest were reported.
result: Use of GLP-1 receptor agonists for 1 to 3 years was associated with increased risk of all thyroid cancer (adjusted hazard ratio 1.58, 95% CI 1.27 to 1.95) and medullary thyroid cancer (1.78, 1.04 to 3.05). This study prompted the EMA signal assessment.
